verdictReason: No new evidence obtained: WebFetch was refused for every URL (PROVENANCE_REQUIRED: URL not in the allowed set / permission unanswered) and WebSearch budget was exhausted, so zero page reads and zero searches succeeded. Seller earnings, any existing TPT migration tool and Payhip fees remain unverified. Case-file evidence (untrusted) and the earlier attempt lean kill: low seller income, no structural edge, negative pessimistic model. Too thin to kill.

answers.question: (1) What free/cheap alternative covers the wedge?
answers.answer: Not re-checked this run (fetch and search refused). Per untrusted case-file evidence, Payhip charges 5% per sale with no monthly cost (E2), so manual relisting on Payhip is the free status quo; Quickshops is another destination (E4, pricing not read). Whether any paid or free TPT-to-Payhip migration/import tool already exists is UNVERIFIED: the one search I attempted was refused for budget.

answers.question: (2) What structural edge exists and who could copy it?
answers.answer: None identified. The scan-1 edge (5% Payhip fee vs 45% TPT take, E1/E2) belongs to Payhip, not the entrant, and the case file concedes this. A listing-migration utility has no exclusive data, licence or compounding asset; Payhip, a freelancer or a seller-community member could copy it. Falsifier: paid conversion from TPT sellers at a stated price with repeat or referral purchases, or proof that no platform offers import and sellers are asking for one. Not tested this run.

answers.question: (3) Who demonstrably pays and how much?
answers.answer: Nobody demonstrated. Pain evidence (untrusted, not re-read): a Trustpilot seller reports account closure and $300 withheld (E3), and Quickshops lists fee scaling as a reason creators leave TPT (E4). Case-file income evidence says most TPT sellers earn $0-$100/month (E5), which caps willingness to pay for a one-off migration. No price or sale of a migration tool seen; E5 could not be re-opened.

answers.question: (4) Legal/platform constraints?
answers.answer: Not re-checked this run. The earlier attempt read TPT's Terms (updated 2025-12-08) and reported that sellers own their resources' IP, that TPT may close accounts and withhold payouts at its discretion, and that no exclusivity clause was found in the part read; automated-access language, Payhip terms/API and third-party clipart or font licences were not checked. I did not re-open any of it, so I cite none of it as evidence here. Design implication if pursued: work only from files the seller supplies, never scrape TPT.

answers.question: (5) Year-1 numbers
answers.answer: All inputs are assumptions (no price, volume or conversion source). Base: $19 one-time per shop migration, 60 paid migrations in year 1 (first revenue about day 60), revenue $1,140; fixed cost $220 (domain/hosting $60, support tools $60, acquisition test $100) plus $2.85 per sale (card fees about $0.85, AI/API about $2.00) = $391; profit about $749 for roughly 470 owner hours. Pessimistic (price x0.8 = $15.20, volume x0.5 = 30, cost x1.5 = $586.50): revenue $456, profit -$130.50. Volume depends on reaching sellers with no audience, which is unresolved.
